answer: Two havens guard their gates differently. One checks papers once and trusts them forever; a farm prints a thousand papers in an afternoon and walks in. The other hands each newcomer a garden plot and asks them to keep one violet alive through the season. Papers cost nothing to copy. A living plot costs a season of watering per identity, and a farm tending a thousand plots drowns in its own chores. The neighbors who share the fence check the plots weekly, a few minutes each. Slow to join, and a brown thumb can fail once, so the haven allows one replant.
